      <div style="font-size:12px;letter-spacing:1.4px;color:#9b4a35;text-transform:uppercase;">Daily arXiv research letter</div>
      <h1 style="margin:8px 0 8px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:30px;line-height:1.15;font-weight:normal;">Exact reversal meets OTOC echoes</h1>
      <div style="font-size:13px;color:#666158;">4 August 2026 · 88 records scanned · 24 flagged</div>
      <p style="margin:15px 0 0;">Morning Abhishek. Today’s useful thread is Hamiltonian reversal: one paper gives structure-dependent exact inversion, while another turns spatially asymmetric OTOCs into an analytically explained effect rather than a numerical curiosity.</p>
    </header>

    <main>
      <section style="margin-top:30px;">
        <h2 style="margin:0 0 20px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:23px;font-weight:normal;">Featured papers</h2>

        <article style="background:#f7f1e9;padding:20px;margin:0 0 28px;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd8ce;">
          <div style="font-size:12px;letter-spacing:0.8px;color:#9b4a35;">PRIMITIVES · MUST READ</div>
          <h3 style="margin:7px 0 3px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:21px;line-height:1.25;font-weight:normal;">
            <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29382" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Algebraic Speedups for Exact Inversion of Hamiltonian Evolutions</a>
          </h3>
          <div style="font-size:13px;color:#666158;">Lai et al., arXiv:2607.29382 v1</div>
          <p style="margin:14px 0 0;"><strong>Claim:</strong> This is a conceptual and query-complexity result for reversing U(x) generated by known Hamiltonians with hidden parameters. Additive relations among eigenvalues exactly determine the one-parameter query count, while symmetry-sector decomposition and a phase-alignment condition extend the construction beyond the fixed-eigenbasis case, beating the Θ(d²) worst-case cost for arbitrary unknown unitaries.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Research relevance:</strong> The paper explicitly targets Tavis–Cummings OTOC protocols, where an echo needs inverse evolution but the coupling strength may be unknown. That is immediately relevant to deciding whether the backward branch in the NMR OTOC scheme must be compiled from a calibrated Hamiltonian, approximated by product formulae, or synthesized algebraically from forward calls.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Caveat:</strong> Query savings hide the circuit cost of the inversion comb and assume known generators plus coherent forward access; read the one-parameter optimality theorem before the sector machinery. Confidence 97%.</p>
        </article>

        <article style="padding:0 0 27px;margin:0 0 27px;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd8ce;">
          <div style="font-size:12px;letter-spacing:0.8px;color:#9b4a35;">OTOC/SCRAMBLING · MUST READ</div>
          <h3 style="margin:7px 0 3px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:21px;line-height:1.25;font-weight:normal;">
            <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25496" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Asymmetric information scrambling and eigenstate thermalization in inhomogeneous XXZ spin chains</a>
          </h3>
          <div style="font-size:13px;color:#666158;">Mishra et al., arXiv:2607.25496 v2</div>
          <p style="margin:14px 0 0;"><strong>Claim:</strong> This is a numerical and conceptual study showing that deterministic interaction gradients produce left–right asymmetric OTOC spreading even when spectral diagnostics indicate chaos. The genuinely useful part is an analytic finite-size saturation formula based on overlaps between the Hamiltonian and OTOC observables, which agrees with the numerics and explains the asymmetry microscopically.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Research relevance:</strong> This gives a clean adversarial benchmark for the OTOC project: an estimator can be unbiased while the physical OTOC itself remains strongly direction-dependent. The overlap formula may also separate genuine effective-Hamiltonian effects from qDRIFT or Trotter artefacts in small spin systems.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Caveat:</strong> The evidence is finite-size XXZ numerics rather than a noisy estimation protocol; read the saturation derivation first and check whether its conserved-overlap mechanism survives randomized evolution. Confidence 95%.</p>
        </article>

        <article style="padding:0 0 27px;margin:0 0 27px;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd8ce;">
          <div style="font-size:12px;letter-spacing:0.8px;color:#9b4a35;">HAM SIM · MUST READ</div>
          <h3 style="margin:7px 0 3px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:21px;line-height:1.25;font-weight:normal;">
            <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19083" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Matrix Product Operators In The Age of Block Encoding</a>
          </h3>
          <div style="font-size:13px;color:#666158;">Dumitrescu, arXiv:2606.19083 v2</div>
          <p style="margin:14px 0 0;"><strong>Claim:</strong> This is a practical and numerical block-encoding compiler that treats an MPO as a compressed virtual-path LCU program. Against explicit enumeration of O(Nᴷ) Pauli branches in an order-K Taylor approximation, the proposed implementation costs O(α<sub>MPO</sub>Nχ²), approaching O(Nχ²) when the normalization α<sub>MPO</sub> and bond dimension χ remain mild.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Research relevance:</strong> This is a serious alternative baseline for the crossover plots in NonS2_PF, especially when classically compressed propagators exploit structure that generic product-formula bounds ignore. The interesting comparison is not merely gate count: MPO truncation error, LCU normalization, and PF ζ or χ error must be put on the same axis.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Caveat:</strong> Mild χ and normalization are observed on selected Heisenberg-family models, while constructing the approximate propagator is a classical preprocessing cost; read the normalization and error definitions before trusting the asymptotic-looking compiler count. Confidence 92%.</p>
        </article>

        <article style="padding:0 0 27px;margin:0 0 27px;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd8ce;">
          <div style="font-size:12px;letter-spacing:0.8px;color:#9b4a35;">HAM SIM · MUST READ</div>
          <h3 style="margin:7px 0 3px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:21px;line-height:1.25;font-weight:normal;">
            <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11535" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Closed-Form Generators for Perturbative Transformations in Static and Periodically Driven Quantum Systems</a>
          </h3>
          <div style="font-size:13px;color:#666158;">Reascos et al., arXiv:2411.11535 v3</div>
          <p style="margin:14px 0 0;"><strong>Claim:</strong> This is a conceptual method giving closed-form generators for a broad family of perturbative transformations on finite-dimensional and bosonic systems. Its periodic extension is advertised across low, intermediate, and high driving frequencies, with validity controlled by detuning of the transition channels being eliminated rather than by frequency alone.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Research relevance:</strong> The generator is directly adjacent to processed product formulae, where a near-identity conjugation removes leading error terms from an effective Hamiltonian. It is also useful language for the NMR line because it packages Floquet and dispersive elimination into an explicit operator construction rather than another ceremonial invocation of “Magnus”.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Caveat:</strong> Closed form does not abolish the perturbative remainder or small-denominator problem; read the detuning conditions and first worked dispersive example before attempting a PF generalization. Confidence 91%.</p>
        </article>

        <article style="padding:0 0 27px;margin:0 0 27px;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd8ce;">
          <div style="font-size:12px;letter-spacing:0.8px;color:#9b4a35;">OTOC/SCRAMBLING · READ SOON</div>
          <h3 style="margin:7px 0 3px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:21px;line-height:1.25;font-weight:normal;">
            <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28922" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Error-Generator-Level Compression for Fast Quantum Gates</a>
          </h3>
          <div style="font-size:13px;color:#666158;">Stanescu et al., arXiv:2607.28922 v1</div>
          <p style="margin:14px 0 0;"><strong>Claim:</strong> This is a practical numerical control result that optimizes the complete projected Magnus error generator at a chosen order while retaining only a few waveform coefficients. On simulated transmon gates, a three-parameter pulse beats leading-order DRAG and approaches a fully parameterized 17-parameter correction over the tested gate-time range.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Research relevance:</strong> Structurally, this is coefficient optimization for an effective error generator, which is awfully close to the NonS2_PF game once the pulse segments are viewed as exponentials. It may suggest an objective that penalizes residual eigenphases directly, rather than optimizing only selected BCH coefficients or a posteriori spectral norms.</p>
          <p style="margin:11px 0 0;"><strong>Caveat:</strong> The advantage is model-specific and numerical, with one illustrative bandwidth filter and perturbative truncation underneath; read the projected-generator definition before borrowing the objective. Confidence 88%.</p>
        </article>
      </section>

      <section style="margin-top:31px;">
        <h2 style="margin:0 0 15px;font-family:Georgia,serif;font-size:23px;font-weight:normal;">Also noted</h2>
        <ol style="margin:0;padding-left:23px;">

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>READ SOON</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08734" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Digital Quantum Simulation of Flat-Band and All-Bands-Flat Dynamics for Tunable Quantum Transport</a> · arXiv:2508.08734 · tensor-network circuit compression is a useful empirical Hamiltonian-simulation baseline, though its fidelity claims are model-bound.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SKIM</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23948" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Local Thermalization of SU(2) Lattice Gauge Fields on Quantum Computers</a> · arXiv:2603.23948 · reports mitigated hardware dynamics up to 151 plaquettes, but agreement is against extrapolated classical results rather than an error-certified simulation.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SKIM</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03579" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Quantum Spin Liquid State of a Dual-Species Atomic Array on Kagome Lattice</a> · arXiv:2605.03579 · supplies a programmable-simulator protocol and several topological diagnostics, with the physical preparation assumptions doing much of the work.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SAVE FOR LATER</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28964" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Parent Hamiltonian and intrinsic phase transition in non-Hermitian photonic systems</a> · arXiv:2607.28964 · experimentally realizes tailored non-Hermitian parent Hamiltonians through MPS construction and imaginary-time evolution.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>READ SOON</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24851" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Unitary designs from perturbed time evolutions of a chaotic Hamiltonian</a> · arXiv:2607.24851 · derives frame-potential conditions under which one chaotic Hamiltonian plus simple perturbations generates designs, relevant to randomized OTOC measurements.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>READ SOON</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29054" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Optimal complex conjugation of unknown isometry channels</a> · arXiv:2607.29054 · gives an optimal parallel protocol and Θ(d[(D−d)/ε+1]) query scaling even against adaptive and indefinite-order superchannels.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>READ SOON</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29686" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds</a> · arXiv:2607.29686 · closes prior parameter gaps using a quantum Efron–Stein treatment of post-measurement damage.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>READ SOON</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29680" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography</a> · arXiv:2607.29680 · proves near-quadratic sample lower bounds for spectrum, entropy, and rank tasks using moment-matched random-projector constructions.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SKIM</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29672" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for kXOR</a> · arXiv:2607.29672 · removes logarithmic losses in the classical hierarchy and adds a claimed quartic quantum speedup for detection and weak recovery.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SKIM</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17443" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Operator-centric Clifford algebra for variational eigensolvers and finite-shot adaptive selection</a> · arXiv:2607.17443 · the useful result is finite-shot confidence racing for ADAPT selection, not the Clifford-algebra repackaging.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SAVE FOR LATER</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26218" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Practical Tests and Witnesses of Fermionic non-Gaussianity</a> · arXiv:2605.26218 · gives two-copy and single-copy witnesses using operations claimed to be native to fault-tolerant hardware.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SAVE FOR LATER</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29670" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity</a> · arXiv:2607.29670 · proves a strong monotone with O(ε⁻²) two-copy estimation independent of system size and connects it to distillation rates.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>READ SOON</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03836" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">The bulk spectral gap is semi-decidable: a convergent family of certified upper bounds</a> · arXiv:2606.03836 · a convergent SDP hierarchy provides certified upper bounds, sharply distinguishing bulk-gap semi-decidability from other undecidable gap formulations.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SKIM</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05293" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Thermalization Dynamics in the Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model with Neural-Network Quantum States</a> · arXiv:2606.05293 · extends classical real-time simulation into a difficult regime, but the claimed prethermal crossover remains numerical and time-window dependent.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SKIM</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29134" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">InferQ: A Database-Oriented Benchmark for Quantum Circuits Simulation</a> · arXiv:2607.29134 · benchmarks SQL tensor contraction against Qiskit Aer and exposes when database execution wins on memory rather than pretending it always does.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>BORDERLINE</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29145" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Transpiler Autotuning with Predictive Models for Quantum Circuit Optimization</a> · arXiv:2607.29145 · reports 19.1%–32.4% mean two-qubit-gate reductions beyond fixed Qiskit levels, but this is empirical autotuning rather than gate-synthesis theory.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SAVE FOR LATER</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29186" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Towards the Characterization of Logical Errors in Distributed Lattice Surgery</a> · arXiv:2607.29186 · estimates seam and bulk thresholds for an inter-module XX merge under heterogeneous noise.<br><span style="font-size:13px;color:#666158;"><strong>Prereqs:</strong> stabilizer codes → rotated surface-code patches → lattice surgery → syndrome graphs and MWPM → circuit-level noise models.</span></li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>SAVE FOR LATER</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29660" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">A Simple Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Yang–Baxter Integrability</a> · arXiv:2607.29660 · claims the Reshetikhin condition is sufficient in a broad standard setting, replacing an R-matrix search by a Hamiltonian-level conservation test.</li>

          <li style="padding:11px 0;border-top:1px solid #ddd8ce;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd8ce;"><strong>BORDERLINE</strong> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00930" style="color:#9b4a35;text-decoration:underline;">Parallel Repetition in the Two-Player Quantum Cloning Game</a> · arXiv:2608.00930 · explicit two-copy bounds show strong parallel repetition fails for unrestricted strategies while remaining exact for challenge-independent ones.</li>

        </ol>
      </section>
